Purpose and exclusions

Small server-owned zone events create shared activity without requiring an ecosystem simulator. Ambient villagers/fishers can animate locally; schedules that change service availability require authoritative time and recovery rules.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Author Riverwatch event: defend the road warning post and deliver repair supplies. Reuse encounter/quest/item definitions with event-cycle context.
  2. Place BP_WorldEventController and NPC_AmbientFisher, a nonrewarding ambient visual actor unless explicitly promoted to a service.
  3. Bind notification/map/quest UI to event phase and server time.
  4. Create schedule table with Day/Night location IDs only after path/door/streaming tests; keep scheduling disabled in the first implementation.
  5. Test overlapping event/resource quotas and restart at resolving phase.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in World events, ambient villagers and later schedules. Rule owner: URPGWorldEventComponent. This asset’s role is Small server-owned zone events create shared activity without requiring an ecosystem simulator. Ambient villagers/fishers can animate locally; schedules that change service availability require authoritative time and recovery rules.

  1. Server time/controller selects a permitted event cycle and records start/end/phase.
  2. Event spawns bounded encounters or requests deliveries through existing systems; it does not implement separate loot/inventory rules.
  3. Verified participation events create eligibility; completion grants rewards once per cycle through the common transaction service.
  4. Clients receive phase/timer/marker cues and ambient effects. Late joiners see current state, not a history of reward notifications.
  5. On restart resume/cancel the recorded cycle under policy without creating a new reward cycle implicitly.
  6. Later NPC schedules move via navigation to authored locations; critical services keep a fallback contact/location so day/night does not strand progression.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Event_Riverwatch / NPC_AmbientFisher. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Replay participation/reward -> one count/grant.
Server restarts -> same cycle or explicit canceled result, not a fresh farmable reward.
Scheduled NPC path blocked -> fallback service remains accessible; no teleport through players/geometry.
Ambient animation notify -> no fish/items spawned into economy.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
